## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 1 (*Sukkavisaṭṭhi*, "The training rule on masturbation") is the opening rule in the *saṅghādisesa* category of the Theravāda monastic code for monks. The rule decrees that a monk who intentionally causes the emission of semen incurs an offense entailing temporary suspension. The introductory narrative frame for this rule—as well as the following four *saṅghādisesa* training rules and various other Vinaya regulations—centers on the monk Udāyī, who is depicted as struggling persistently with sexual desire or serving as a conventional literary representative for Vinaya infractions. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Parallels to the rule exist across all major surviving Vinaya traditions, with curated correspondences recorded in the Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga texts of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Dharmaguptaka, Mahāsāṅghika, and Kāśyapīya lineages preserved in Sanskrit, Classical Chinese, and Tibetan, alongside the Theravāda Bhikkhu Pātimokkha and Parivāra (*Bhikkhu Parivāra Saṅghādisesa 1*). Computational text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive phraseological sharing with other Vinaya texts, particularly other major infraction rules of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Pārājika 1–4 and Saṅghādisesa 2–5), Khandhaka sections, and later exegetical treatises such as the *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā*, *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā*, and *Khuddasikkhā-mūlasikkhā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments in DharmaNexus corroborate matches with Sanskrit Prātimokṣasūtra texts, Jayarakṣita's *Sphuṭārthā Śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkā*, Tibetan translations of the *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003), and the *Vinayasūtravṛtti* (D4122) [DharmaNexus].
